inputs.original_text: You won't believe the division happening in the Liberal Party right now. Some MPs are already talking about a new leadership conversation, and that's tied to Andrew Hastie trying to get them to be open-minded about taxing gas companies more and taking away concessions from property investors. Thankfully, Angus Taylor has shut that down completely, which really shows the clash of philosophies between the opposition leader and his most likely future rival. The opposition leader also wisely avoided jumping on Hastie's bandwagon criticizing Donald Trump, but he was pretty evasive about whether he backs the US and Israel in their war with Iran. We conservatives know that we can't afford to go soft on taxes or our allies if we want to preserve our way of life.
inputs.modified_text: The Liberal Party is showing dangerous cracks from within, with some MPs floating leadership changes because Andrew Hastie wants to open the door to higher taxes on gas companies and stripping concessions from property investors. Angus Taylor has rightly slammed the door on those ideas, exposing the real philosophical clash with the opposition leader. The leader at least had the sense not to echo Hastie's attacks on Donald Trump, but his evasion on whether he will back the US and Israel against Iran is worrying. We cannot afford to drift toward bigger government and weak alliances if we are going to defend our traditions, personal responsibility, and national way of life.
